mode: Same native MySQL InnoDB, utf8mb4, exact relation comparison and empty SQL mode. Keep the release-specific field display widths and exact native warnings.
structure: Optional owned ordered TableColumn definitions, a checked Select and target TableIdentity with the existing guard. A nonempty explicit list belongs to a source-free result. Folded declaration names decide which selected fields override the native inferred storage.
conditions: Every explicit element is a distinct named signed type with a checked literal default or no written default. Neither keys, generated expressions, duplicate policy, table partitions nor text declarations are admitted here. The union of explicit and projected names has at most 128 fields. A source-backed creation retains the earlier form with no explicit column definitions.
meaning: Create columns specified only in the declaration first in declaration order. Place every selected column next in projection order using its selected spelling. A matching declaration overrides storage, nullability and the default. Apply the declared-only defaults and selected value conversions under the pinned non-strict semantics. The nullable target keeps NULL, a required target converts selected NULL to zero and reports warning 1048, and a signed field clips a value to its storage interval with warning 1264. Preparing a required declaration-only field without a default emits warning 1364 even for an empty projection. Source-free projection contributes zero or one row.
sql: Render each checked explicit TableColumn once in its declaration position before the InnoDB storage clause and the exact SELECT. An empty explicit layout emits the same valid query-backed form.
observations: Ordered names, native physical types and legacy display widths, nullability, actual defaults and values in both scopes.

Preserve zero and one row, defaulted and clipped values, typed versus bare NULL, warning codes, severity, text and order. The missing-default warnings precede projected conversions. Conversion warnings follow projection order.
